A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the frequency of AGN activity at the centers of galaxy groups, and the properties of their host galaxies, is consistent with the AGN population in the general galaxy population, with no strong dependence on halo-centric distance.

the frequency of AGN activity, as probed by X-rays, in group halos of this redshift and mass range appears to be independent of halo-centric distance and halo mass, but is strongly dependent on galaxy mass, with central galaxies being more likely to host low-to-moderately luminous AGNs.

AGN activity in groups is a natural consequence of the AGN activity in galaxies, with no evidence for a dependence of the AGN frequency on halo-centric distance or halo-centric mass, but a weak dependence on halo mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency of low-level AGN activity in galaxies is a strong function of mass and that, at least for galaxy group halos, the AGN population is dominated by central galaxies.
the AGN population in galaxy groups is a reflection of the global population, and that AGNs are not preferentially hosted by galaxies residing in the inner regions of group halos.
the X-ray luminosity function of AGNs in galaxy groups is consistent with that of the field population, suggesting that AGN activity in groups is not significantly affected by the group environment.
